deep.reconstruction:
This is a numbered list of open questions in the homotopy theory of categories and presheaf categories. The vocabulary (test categories, (elementary) modelizers, the class W of weak equivalences, Hot_W, asphericity, contractibility structures) is that of Pursuing Stacks (1983). The archive date '[à partir de 1973]' is probably too early for this content: the 1973 date comes from the reused letter-head on the verso of the next page.

Item by item:
(1) Do 'Čech-type' asphericity conditions hold? A plausible reading is a criterion of the form 'if every finite intersection, or fibre product, of covering objects is aspherical, then the union is aspherical'. Is this implied by a previously listed statement 'L 5'?
(2) Are the class W of weak equivalences in Cat and the induced class W_A in the presheaf category Â saturated? Saturated means a map is in W iff it becomes invertible in the localization.
(3) Homotopy properties of (Cat), Dold-Puppe sequences in (Cat), and whether (Cat) is a Quillen model category. Thomason answered the last part in 1980.
(4)/(5) These two items are renumbered (crossed-out digits and an arrow).
- When is Â a (closed) model category, i.e. for which (test) categories A does the presheaf category carry a model structure with weak equivalences W_A? Cisinski later answered this in general.
- Exactness properties of Hot_W and of the localization functors Cat → Hot_W and Â → Hot_W. This concerns which homotopy limits and colimits exist and are preserved, i.e. the germ of derivator theory.
(6) Is Δ° (the opposite of the simplex category) a test category, or a weak test category? Grothendieck answers 'no'.
- (a) Look at variants: Δf (presumably the category of finite ordinals with injective maps, giving semi-simplicial sets), and several categories of finite ordered sets, O^f, Õ, O_f.
- (b) The 'cubical game': which cube categories are test categories.
(7) (Commutative) cohomological invariants of Â when A is an elementary modelizer. Can the Dold-Puppe (Dold-Kan) correspondence be axiomatized beyond Δ? Test case: the category O (finite ordered sets?).
(8) The integral ∫ of a diagram of homotopy types, defined as a homotopy colimit, together with the dual notion (homotopy limit). An intrinsic 'homotopy category' structure on Hot and similar categories, plus a contractibility structure. These are precursors of derivators and of the 'contractors' and 'contractibility structures' of Pursuing Stacks.
(9) Topological spaces as a modelizer: test functors A → Top and geometric realization.
(10) Pointed homotopy types and group objects. If (M,W) is a (strict) modelizer, is Gr(M), with weak equivalences detected on underlying objects, a modelizer for pointed 0-connected homotopy types? Is this tied up with Dold-Puppe?
- The model cases for a positive answer are classical: Kan's loop group (M = simplicial sets) and topological groups (M = Top, via Milnor).

Purpose: to organize the programme that became Pursuing Stacks, Part II ('test categories and modelizers'), and later Les Dérivateurs.
errors: Question 10 as stated has a negative answer in general. M = (Cat) with Thomason weak equivalences is a (strict) modelizer. But group objects in Cat are strict 2-groups (equivalently crossed modules, Brown-Spencer 1976). Their underlying categories are groupoids, so Gr(Cat) localized at W models only pointed connected homotopy 2-types, not all pointed 0-connected types. Hence the hypothesis 'M a strict modelizer' is insufficient; something like a presheaf modelizer with good products (simplicial sets à la Kan) is needed. The parenthetical '(strict?)' suggests Grothendieck sensed the condition was delicate.
Item 1 is too elliptic ('implied by L 5)?') to check: the referent of 'L 5' is not on the page.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a question list matching the programme of Pursuing Stacks, Part II. Almost every item reappears there or was later resolved by Thomason, Cisinski, Maltsiniotis or Lack-Street. The page is mostly of dating and historical interest: it is probably closer to 1983 than to 1973.
